name: Morocco
summary: Four thousand metres of High Atlas within three hours of the Atlantic, four imperial cities, and the edge of the Sahara at Merzouga — a country you can cross from surf to dunes in two days.

entries.caption: Where the Atlas Meets the Sahara
entries.description: Snow on the High Atlas in the morning and the first dunes of the Sahara by evening.
entries.subject: the High Atlas mountains rising behind a Moroccan kasbah

entries.caption: The Draa and the Dades
entries.description: Palm oases strung along the Draa, and gorges cut red through the Dades and the Todra.
entries.subject: the Todra gorge with red rock walls and a river below

entries.caption: Barbary Macaques and the Argan Forest
entries.description: Macaques in the cedar forest above Azrou, and goats standing in the argan trees near Essaouira.
entries.subject: Barbary macaques in the cedar forest of the Middle Atlas

entries.caption: Desert Country
entries.description: Not the safari of the east — the wildlife here is desert-adapted, and you look for it at first light.
entries.subject: a desert track through stony hammada in southern Morocco

entries.caption: The High Atlas
entries.description: Toubkal is 4,167 metres and the highest point in North Africa, walkable in two days from Imlil.
entries.subject: Mount Toubkal under snow above the village of Imlil

entries.caption: Ouzoud
entries.description: A hundred metres of water in three stages, with macaques in the olive trees beside it.
entries.subject: the Ouzoud falls dropping in stages through olive trees

entries.caption: The Draa River
entries.description: The longest river in Morocco, mostly dry, and green the whole way where it is not.
entries.subject: palm groves along the Draa valley in southern Morocco

entries.caption: The Atlantic Coast
entries.description: Essaouira's wind, Taghazout's point breaks, and the long empty beaches between them.
entries.subject: the walled seafront of Essaouira with fishing boats

entries.caption: The Cedar Forest
entries.description: The Middle Atlas cedar, some of it a thousand years old, above Ifrane and Azrou.
entries.subject: ancient Atlas cedar trees in the Middle Atlas forest

entries.caption: Dunes, Gorges and Surf
entries.description: Trekking in the Atlas, surfing the Atlantic points, and a night out on the erg at Chegaga.
entries.subject: a trekking trail high on a ridge in the High Atlas

entries.caption: Amazigh and Arab
entries.description: Three Amazigh languages, Arabic, French and Spanish, and a culture that predates all of them.
entries.subject: an Amazigh village of earth houses built into a hillside

entries.caption: The People of the Atlas
entries.description: Village life at two thousand metres, where the year is still organised around the snow.
entries.subject: a shepherd with his flock on a High Atlas terrace

entries.caption: Tagine, Bread and Mint
entries.description: Slow-cooked tagine, bread baked in the neighbourhood oven, and tea poured from height.
entries.subject: a tagine cooking over charcoal at a roadside stall

entries.caption: Moussem and Gnaoua
entries.description: The Gnaoua festival in Essaouira in June, and the moussems that mark the harvest.
entries.subject: musicians playing at the Gnaoua festival in Essaouira

entries.caption: Zellige, Leather and Wool
entries.description: Tile cut by hand in Fez, tanned leather, and carpets woven to patterns held in memory.
entries.subject: a craftsman cutting zellige tile by hand in Fez

entries.caption: Volubilis and the Kasbahs
entries.description: A Roman city on the plain at Volubilis, and Ait Benhaddou standing above the Ounila.
entries.subject: the earth kasbah of Ait Benhaddou above the river

entries.caption: The Imperial Cities
entries.description: Fez, Marrakesh, Meknes and Rabat — four capitals, each of a different dynasty.
entries.subject: the tanneries and rooftops of the Fez medina

entries.caption: Marrakesh and Casablanca
entries.description: Jemaa el-Fnaa at dusk, and the Atlantic modernism of Casablanca an hour up the road.
entries.subject: Jemaa el-Fnaa square in Marrakesh filling at dusk

entries.caption: Riad and Medina
entries.description: Rooms built inward around a courtyard, because the street was never meant to see in.
entries.subject: the tiled courtyard of a traditional Moroccan riad

entries.caption: The Souk in the Morning
entries.description: Before the tour groups, the medina is simply where people buy their vegetables.
entries.subject: a produce market in a Moroccan medina early in the morning

entries.caption: Easy Travelling
entries.description: Short drives, good roads, and a train line down the coast that children enjoy.
entries.subject: a family walking a quiet lane in a Moroccan hill village

entries.caption: Trek, Surf, Ride
entries.description: Multi-day Atlas treks, Atlantic surf schools, and horses on the Essaouira sand.
entries.subject: surfers walking the beach at Taghazout at sunset

entries.caption: Desert Camps and Riads
entries.description: Erg Chigaga camps well beyond the day-trip dunes, and riads restored room by room.
entries.subject: a desert camp of tents on the dunes at Erg Chigaga

entries.caption: Oasis Agriculture
entries.description: The khettara irrigation channels still working, and the argan cooperatives run by women.
entries.subject: a palm oasis irrigated by traditional channels

entries.caption: Light on Earth Walls
entries.description: Pisé takes late light the way nothing else does, which is why every photographer comes here.
entries.subject: late light on the earth walls of a southern Moroccan kasbah

entries.caption: Chefchaouen and the Rif
entries.description: The blue town in the Rif, and a mountain range most itineraries drive straight past.
entries.subject: the blue-painted lanes of Chefchaouen in the Rif

entries.caption: Two Days, Four Climates
entries.description: Surf in the morning, cedar forest by lunch, and the Sahara the following evening.
entries.subject: a road climbing a High Atlas pass with the Sahara beyond
